svg.aria-label: Real output of rls_check v0.1.0 on examples/grant-fix

g.text: $ python3 rls_check.py examples/grant-fix
Supabase RLS pre-launch check v0.1.0 - examples/grant-fix
Read 2 SQL file(s) and 0 app source file(s); 1 table(s) in exposed schema(s): public
table public.invoices
[CRITICAL] RLS001 Table has no row level security
where: supabase/migrations/20261102090000_invoices.sql:1
why: Without RLS, any API role with privileges on this table can read and change every row.
Supabase projects created before 30 May 2026 gave anon those privileges automatically on
every table made before 30 Oct 2026, and any later GRANT does the same; the anon key ships
in your frontend.
fix: alter table public.invoices enable row level security;
create policy "invoices_owner_all" on public.invoices for all to authenticated using
((select auth.uid()) = user_id) with check ((select auth.uid()) = user_id);
schema public
[HIGH] GRANT002 Schema-wide grant to anon, authenticated on all tables
where: supabase/migrations/20261102093000_fix_permission_denied.sql:2
why: Every table that existed at this point became reachable through the Data API for anon,
authenticated, including 1 without RLS (public.invoices), so all their rows are open.
fix: revoke all on all tables in schema public from anon, authenticated; -- then grant each
table only what the app needs, after RLS and its policies exist, e.g. grant select, insert,
update, delete on public.<table> to authenticated;
Summary: 1 critical, 1 high, 0 medium, 0 low -> FAIL (fail-on: high)
Limits: Static reading of migration files only: changes made in the Supabase dashboard are invisible to
this tool, and it does not test policies against a live database or replace a human review.
$ echo $?
